title: (wrong behaviour after a hitch): a movie's subtitle line starts only when the shown frame equals its start frame (MoviePlayingSequence.cpp:335-350), and a movie rumble the same way (DemoPadRumbler.cpp:23-30). The shown frame is picked from the sound's place and frames are passed over when the game is a whole frame late (MovieStream.cpp:194-217, MovieStream.hpp:50-54), so a hitch at that moment loses the line or the rumble for good. The frame is also picked inside MoviePlayerSimple::draw (:72-74), so what the step reads depends on when the draw ran.
note: Found by the inventory's pass two (the Game/Screen whole read, 11-18, every line cited read at 6577392b5). Modern form: each entry fires when the movie's place crosses its start (last < start <= now), read from the movie position, not the picked picture; the pick moves to the step (or the host) and the draw only shows it. Test: a forced late step over a start frame still shows the line and rumbles.

title: (console-era remnant, audio sync): the staff roll is timed by counting game steps beside the music: pictures at fixed steps (StaffRoll.cpp:49-56, :178-187), mBgmFrame counted per step while the music plays (:552-554), and the end logo when that count reaches 14211 less the scroll's steps (:387-395). A late audio buffer or a hitch moves the pictures and the end off the music.
note: Found by the inventory's pass two (the Game/Screen whole read, 11-18, every line cited read at 6577392b5). Same file, 5.H.3 small (P-208): 64 line layouts with the rest of a line dropped (:283-288, :691-695) and 20 pictures (:27, :193-204).

title: (the console Mii format's rules decide which Miis are offered; question for the owner): a Mii is known by the console format's 8-byte create ID and its flag bits (MiiCharacters.cpp:22-24, :156-182): an ID of zeros is none, a temporary ID (bit 0x20) never matches another, and a special Mii (bit 0x80 clear) is refused unless it is marked local-only (:202); nebula_game_mii_valid applies the same rules for the host (:221-224).
note: Found by the readall harness's Game/Mii report (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. Proposed: the host's library gives each Mii a stable identity of its own and checks the record once at import; the create ID stays as the key old console saves carry. Question: keep or drop the special and local-only refusal? Replay: the game's steps are the same; which Miis are offered may change. Owner 11-19: drop the refusal: special Miis can be imported.

title: (the host's menus, stability and one console number): the benchmark menu reads a result file into a buffer of the most it allows, 16 MiB + 1 for frame lists, zero-filled whatever the file's size (file_text, benchmark_menu.cpp:74-84), its results listed, read and drawn under its lock; the render thread's poll_dlss_download reads s_vendor_offer and s_license_pages with no lock and then takes the settings lock that a whole page build holds (native_settings.cpp:5697-5708; s_vendor_offer a plain enum, :5486); save_now waits at most 5 s for the save worker and then writes itself, so two writers can overlap on the settings files (settings_save_model.cpp:93-98); the save worker and the dropped-file Mii import run on detached threads, the worker capturing this and never joined (settings_save_model.cpp:35-36; native_settings.cpp:6529-6538, no try); the YOUR MIIS row shows "%d OF 100" (settings_general_page.cpp:208-210), the Wii database's 100 slots, though the library is a list of any length (mii_import.h:51-57, :61) and the game's picker takes any number (Mii.hpp:3; MiiCharacters.cpp:111).
note: Found by the readall harness's runtime/src/ui report (11-18, read at 0c98b11c2) and checked by reading every line cited at 241395b49. Fixes: the file read by its size on a worker when the page opens, the finished pages handed over under the lock; the download's state published as atomics, the render thread taking no settings lock; every write through the model's one thread, save_now posting a request and waiting for its completion with a bounded, reported timeout, files replaced atomically; workers owned and joined at shutdown, each task catching its own exceptions; the Mii row showing the count alone. The mod import's detached threads (native_settings.cpp:3401-3474) and the ABOUT window's wait (:5953-5966) are mods, out of this order. Replay identical.
